r: "Ford-maker" – one who shows the path across the cycle of rebirth; a **Jain** term
Only the last two, **Parshvanatha (23rd)** and **Mahavira (24th)**, are confirmed by Jain and Buddhist texts; the first 22 are uncertain
**Rishabhadeva (Adinatha / Rishabhanatha)**, born at **Ayodhya** to Nabhi and Marudevi
**Vardhamana Mahavira** – a **reformer** of an older faith, not its founder
**Born at Varanasi** to **King Asvasena and Queen Vama** – associated mainly with **Varanasi**
Renounced at **30**; enlightenment after **84 days** of penance; died at **100**, about **250 years before Mahavira**
**Four vows (chaturyama)**; eternity of matter; his followers wore **white**
**Yashoda**; daughter **Anojja (Priyadarshana)** – Svetambara view; Digambaras say he never married
At **30**; one garment for 13 months, then a naked monk; **12 years** of austerity
At **42**, under a **sal tree** at **Jrimbhikagrama** on the **Rijupalika**
**Pava (Pavapuri)** near Rajgriha, aged **72**; 527 BCE (traditional) or 468 BCE
Mahavira (great hero), **Jina** (conqueror), **Nirgrantha** (free from bonds), Kevalin, Arhat (**Tathagata** is the Buddha's title)
30 years in Kosala, Magadha and further east; first sermon at **Rajgriha**; visited the courts of Bimbisara and Ajatashatru
Chief of the **Lichchhavis** of Vaishali; Mahavira's **maternal uncle** (Trishala was his **sister**); his daughter **Chellana** married Bimbisara
His nephew and son-in-law; **first disciple / follower**
Only **Arya Sudharma** survived him and became the **first Thera (head of the Sangha)**
Contemporary teacher (Parshvanatha was earlier; Bhadrabahu and Chandragupta later)
Companion for about six years; founder of the **Ajivikas** (niyati)
Reality is **many-sided**; no single view holds the whole truth – basis of **tolerance and pluralism**; the **core theory of Jainism**
Relativity of knowledge: every statement is prefixed with **syat** ("maybe", "in some respect") – **conditioned predication**

2.x: **Two main doctrines of Jain philosophy:** Anekantavada and Syadvada. Every thing has many properties, the permanent one being its **attribute (guna)**; everything that exists has **substance (dravya), quality (guna) and mode (paryaya)**.

r: Digambara monk; **propounded / preached Syadvada** and Anekantavada; wrote **Samayasara**, Pravachanasara, Panchastikayasara, Niyamasara; ashram at **Konakondla** (Anantapur); first Jain monk of Andhra
Held the title **"Syadvadachala Simha"**; wrote Yasastilaka Champu, Nitivakyamrita
Jain monk honoured at the Satavahana court (Pratishthana)

3.x: **Right faith (belief), right knowledge, right conduct (action)** – the Jain three jewels.

r: First step of the Buddhist Eightfold Path
**Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha** – the three refuges; Nyaya and Yoga have none

3.x: **Mahavratas** = great vows of monks; **Anuvratas** = small vows of householders – a **Jain** concept. **Householders** also gave cooked food to the needy daily; strict followers avoided **agriculture**.

r: Ritual fast unto death at life's end – **Jain**; Chandragupta Maurya at Shravanabelagola
**Eternal**, with **no final annihilation**; Jainism is non-theistic

4.x: **Souls everywhere:** All objects, even **rocks, stones and running water**, have a soul and feel injury → extreme ahimsa.
**No creator:** The world is **not created** by a supreme being; it runs by an **eternal law** of decay and development – "**Universal Law**"
**Four forms of existence:** **Deva** (gods), **Manushya** (humans), **Naraki** (hell beings), **Tiryancha** (animals and plants)
**Salvation:** Only through **monastic life** – householders cannot attain it; the Vedas and Brahmana supremacy are rejected.

r: Material bondage of the soul, cause of rebirth
**Middle Way** – **avoiding the extremes** of penance and enjoyment

5.x: **Common to both:** **karma and transmigration**, **indifference to the Vedas**, **denial of rituals**, **non-injury to animals**; both were Kshatriya-led shramana movements.
**Not common:** **self-mortification** (Jain only) and **avoiding the extremes** of penance and enjoyment (Buddhist only).
Salvation for both men and women and salvation only after death are not beliefs shared by the two.
**Decline of Jainism:** severe austerities, loss of royal patronage, the Digambara–Svetambara split.

r: Basadi of **Samprati**, Ashoka's grandson ("Ashoka of Jainism"); Kharavela's vihara nearby
"Jain corridor" on the **Bhadrabahu–Chandragupta route** to Shravanabelagola
Prolaraju's record opens with a Jain prayer – the **early Kakatiyas** were Jains
Said to have conquered Andhra and spread Jainism there

6.x: **Ikshvaku** royal women (Chantisiri, Bodhisiri) backed **Buddhism** at Nagarjunakonda.
